title: The roof on hand-over night
question: Tonight the final AI draft goes to Caplet and from tomorrow the IPS is theirs. What did rounds 7 and 8 teach us about how we work, and how should Keel behave while someone else holds the pen?
serves: Creativity & Presentation ('a compelling, well-organized narrative in an authentic team voice') through the hand-over Caplet rewrites from; Ray's 3 Nov ask (I80: Keel overcomplicates, show things plainly); Commandment IV (plain sense)
essence: From tomorrow the draft is yours: rewrite it in your own words, put it through GPTZero because we can't, and submit it by 9 am Saturday 7 November, Sydney time.
Open the README first; it tells you which short card to use when you cut a sentence, change a word or decide the last line.
Send us your rewrite and we'll list anything whose meaning changed, without rewriting a word of it for you; send nothing and we'll stay out of your way.
decided: 3-0: keep the three cards, no merge tonight (Jun and Amara moved in round 2: the look-alike card's 2 of 2 belongs to the card as it stands; 'I wrote that we can't stop touching the page, then asked for a new one at nine o'clock')

3-0: the hand-over README now routes by task (cutting a sentence: the case card; changing a word or fact: the look-alike card; weighing the last sentence or a suggested cut: the readers card) and says 'can dry up'; Tess's two extra fixes ('covered with Treasuries'; 'read an earlier wording', the false 'no false line' gone) went with it. One first-time Year 11 reader, Amara's key and bar sealed first: PASS 6 of 6. 'helped deepen the 1987 crash' (the FINAL's words) swapped in after the test, 2-0. Applied to drafts/FINAL and the project folder

Tess's call: KEEL_RECORD's 'treats Laura's income as a bet on shares already' now gives the FINAL's words; COMMANDMENTS_CHECK gets one bracketed note under 'Applied' (changed later at f06ad13; 495 strict)

3-0 on the lesson, LS-17 (Amara's, aimed at every hand-over file; search and read both): 'Before a changed text is handed over, someone who wrote none of the files beside it searches each, README included, for the old words and old word count, reads every hit, then reads each file through against the handed-over hash.' No hash lesson: the Archive's HEALTH rule already says it

LS-10 2 to 3 by date (P7: four beats, three moves; not bent by design, since Q16 was the whole text), 3-0; LS-15 held on both cuts, 3-0; LS-16 0 to 1, bent (the 7.6 v 10.0 years figure reached Caplet's line before anything was put back; Jun then put three things back and it held: at least 1.83 years short, MODEL), 2 for bent, Amara uncounted; LS-14 stays at 1

3-0: round 9 (Thu 5 Nov) is a freeze: no question, no scouts; every beat reads Caplet's words where they land (INSTRUCTIONS.md, ASK_HUMANS.md's Answer column, their IPS Report Doc, read only) and stops with one line if there is nothing; the Library and the Lab run only on a line Caplet quotes; a rewrite gets one pass from the first beat after it lands, with the Writing Room's sealed key: a list of what moved and both strict counts, never a sentence of ours
seeds: When their rewrite drops a line we fought for, how do we tell a broken fact from a choice that's theirs, and say only the first? (Tess; Friday's run, with fresh eyes)

The first-time reader found the README's summary of the lock ('priced as if money waiting for a cheque earned nothing') hard to follow, though three readers said the IPS's own words back right. Does the Final Report explain the lock in the order a stranger needs: why a ladder reinvests, then what the lock assumes? (Writing Room, from Sun 8 Nov)
